statement: Find the stationary points of $y=\\frac{x}{1+x^{2}}$ and determine their nature. Hence sketch the curve.
solution: $y'=\\frac{(1+x^{2})-x(2x)}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}=\\frac{1-x^{2}}{(1+x^{2})^{2}}$, zero when $x=\\pm 1$. At $x=1$, $y=1/2$ (maximum, since $y'$ changes $+$ to $-$); at $x=-1$, $y=-1/2$ (minimum). The curve passes through the origin with $y\\sim x$ near $0$ and $y\\to 0$ as $x\\to\\pm\\infty$.
hints: Check the sign of $y'$ on either side of $\\pm 1$.
